sections.h2: Technical and legal work in the same team
sections.intro: The people who build your campaign tools and the people who check them against Swiss law work in the same team, so **every tool, advertisement and database is checked before it is used**.

items: We build campaign sites, supporter tools and participation apps ourselves.
We run paid digital campaigns within the rules of each platform.
We use AI to draft, translate and analyse, and a person reviews every result.
We run local and national campaigns, from a seat on a communal council to a federal vote.
We never use deepfakes or synthetic people.
We never target people on the basis of their political opinions.
We keep only the data a purpose needs, hosted in Switzerland or the EU.
We check every campaign item against the law before it is published.

sections.intro: Each service covers one stage of your work: **your profile before the campaign, the campaign itself up to the finance declarations, then your press relations and supporter data before, during and after the vote**.

items.text: A written position, a visual identity, and a website, newsletter and contact lists that you control, so voters know who you are before the campaign starts.
Your election or vote campaign run within the law, from collecting signatures to filing the finance declarations after the vote.
Press relations, media monitoring, answers to false claims and the protection of your supporter data, before, during and after a vote.

sections.h2: From the commune to the Confederation
body: We work at every level where Swiss politics takes place: a seat on a communal council, a cantonal vote, a national initiative. Each level has its own rules, deadlines and media, and a campaign has to follow them.

**Local and multilingual communication is part of every mandate**. Texts for each region are written by native writers who know its vocabulary and its press, so a campaign that crosses a language border reads as if it had been written there.

sections.intro: Political work depends on trust. We handle every mandate so that nothing about it can surprise you in the press.

items.text: We never name a client, show their work or **talk about their mandate without written consent**. Only the people assigned to your mandate can open its files, and we collect only the data it needs, because **what is never collected cannot leak**.

Every item is checked against the law before it is published, every paid message names who paid for it, and every donation is recorded from the first franc. If a journalist asks, **the answer is already documented**.

At the end of the mandate, your contact lists and materials are returned to you or deleted, as you choose. **They are never reused for another client**, including a candidate or committee on the opposing side.

sections.h2: Explain your needs in full confidence
sections.text: Your message is read only by a member of our team, who answers you personally within 3 days. **Nothing you write to us is shared with another client or with the press**, and your details are deleted if no mandate follows. The first exchange commits you to nothing: we tell you plainly whether we can help, or whether you do not need us at all.

offer.title: Services
offer.description: Profile, Campaign and Trust: the three services Tribea offers to parties, candidates and committees in Switzerland.

sections.h1: What we do for parties, candidates and committees
sections.lead: Profile covers the time between campaigns, Campaign the months before a vote, and Trust the press relations and data that run through both. You can start with any of them.

items.text: A written position, a visual identity, a monthly content plan for your website, newsletter and contact lists, and media training.
The campaign plan, signature drives, paid digital campaigns, mobilisation, campaign websites and finance declarations.
Press relations, monitoring, response to false claims, data protection and a legal check of every campaign item.
A separate practice that helps cantons and communes inform citizens objectively and build accessible digital services.

sections.h2: The rules that apply to all three
body: Every service runs on the same method: a legal check before anything is published, an impact assessment before any supporter database is built, and a calendar of the finance declarations your campaign has to file.
Administrations are served by a separate practice with its own team, contracts and data.

sections.text: Tell us which election or vote you are preparing and when it takes place. We will tell you which service fits, or whether you need us at all.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Profile prepares candidates, parties and committees before a campaign: a written position, a visual identity, and a website, newsletter and contact lists they control.

sections.h1: Be known before the campaign starts
sections.lead: Profile prepares candidates, parties and committees before a campaign starts: a written position, a visual identity, and a website, newsletter and contact lists they control.

items.text: One or two pages stating what you stand for, on which issues, and the words you use for them, compared with the words your opponents use for the same issues.
A logo, colours and templates for posters, social media posts and letters, designed for local and multilingual use, from a single commune to the whole country.

A monthly plan saying what is published on your website, in your newsletter and in your messaging groups, when and by whom. These channels reach your contacts directly, whatever a social network changes in its rules.
Preparation for interviews and debates on radio, on television and with local newspapers, with practice sessions recorded and reviewed together.
Over a few weeks we set your position and your visual identity together, with one decision meeting at the end of each week.
A plan agreed each month keeps you visible between campaigns, with every item reviewed before it goes out.
Your brand never borrows the Swiss cross or a cantonal or communal coat of arms, which avoids any suggestion of an official link.
Your contact lists are built on consent, with the date, source and wording of each consent kept on record.

campaign.title: Campaign
campaign.description: Campaign runs election and vote campaigns within Swiss law, from the first analysis of the electorate to the finance declarations filed after the vote.

sections.h1: Run your campaign within the rules
sections.lead: A vote or an election involves signature deadlines, advertising rules and finance declarations spread over several months. Campaign covers all of it, from the first analysis of the electorate to the declarations filed after the vote.

items.text: Targets, messages, channels, budget and calendar on a few pages, agreed with you before any money is spent.
Collection for initiatives and referendums that follows the Federal Chancellery's code of conduct, with trained collectors and checked lists.
Advertising within each platform's rules on political content, with every paid message stating who paid for it.
Reminders and calls to vote sent only to people who agreed to receive them.
Fast, accessible sites with lawful donation forms that record what the finance rules require.
The declarations due to the Swiss Federal Audit Office and to the cantons that have their own rules, prepared on time.

body: Electronic signature collection is being prepared at federal level, and the Swiss electronic identity, the e-ID, was approved by voters on 28 September 2025.
We prepare your campaign for both, so that it can collect signatures and verify supporters online as soon as the law allows it.

items.text: Political opinions are sensitive personal data, and we do not use them to select who sees an advertisement.
items.basis: Federal Act on Data Protection, art. 5

items.text: We never create or publish synthetic images, voices or videos of real people.
Each advertisement names the person or committee that paid for it.
Donations and campaign budgets are recorded from the first franc, so the declaration is written from complete records.

trust.title: Trust
trust.description: Trust covers press relations, media monitoring, answers to false claims, the protection of supporter data and the legal check of every campaign item.

sections.lead: Trust covers the work around a campaign: questions from journalists, false claims that circulate, the security of your supporter data, and the legal check of every item before it is published.

items.text: Media releases, interviews and background briefings for local, regional and national newsrooms, in the language each one publishes in.
A daily watch on the media and social networks that cover your issue, sent as a short written summary.
A fast, documented answer when a fake or a false claim about you circulates, with the evidence to correct it.
The record of processing, the impact assessment and the security measures your databases require.

items.h3: Legal check of every campaign item
items.text: Posters, posts, letters and advertisements are checked against the law before they are published.
One person on our team knows your file and answers when something happens.

items.h3: A response plan agreed in advance
items.text: Who decides, who speaks and what is said is settled before a crisis, so nobody improvises under pressure.
Each month we go through what changed in the media, in the law and in your data, and adjust the plan.

sections.text: We examine your press relations, your supporter data and your campaign materials, and send you a written list of the risks we find, ranked by urgency.

publicSector.title: Public sector
publicSector.description: Tribea's separate public sector practice helps cantons and communes inform citizens objectively and build accessible digital services.

sections.lead: Cantons and communes have to explain votes, projects and services to every resident, in a way that is complete, balanced and accessible. Our public sector practice helps them do that.

items.text: Explanations that present a proposal and its consequences completely and without taking sides, as authorities are required to do.
Websites and online services that meet the WCAG accessibility guidelines and work for people with disabilities.
Texts written by native writers for each commune, region or canton, using the terms your administration already uses.
Consultations and participation apps that collect only the data the purpose needs and publish how the results are used.

sections.h2: How the practice is kept apart
sections.intro: Because we also work for parties and committees, the public sector practice is separated from the rest of the agency by rules we apply to every mandate.

items.text: Only the people assigned to an administration's mandate can open its files.
Mandates follow public procurement rules and are never bundled with work for political clients.
Data from an administration is stored separately and never used for another client.
We do not advise a party or committee on a vote while informing citizens about the same vote for an administration.

sections.text: Tell us about your project, or ask for references from administrations we have worked with.

techPolicy.title: Technology policy
techPolicy.description: What Tribea uses AI and other technology for, who reviews the output, and what the agency refuses to do.

sections.lead: This policy states what we use technology for, who is responsible for the result, and what we refuse to do for any client. It applies to every employee and every mandate.

paras: We use AI tools for three tasks:
list: drafting texts, which a person then rewrites and approves
translating between the national languages, which a native writer then checks
analysing large volumes of public material, such as press coverage or consultation responses

paras: No output of an AI tool is published or sent to a client without being reviewed by a named person on our team. That person is responsible for the result as if they had written it themselves.

list: create synthetic images, voices or videos of real people
present a machine-generated person as real, such as a fictitious supporter or witness
run hidden automation, such as bots posting as if they were citizens
select who sees a political message on the basis of their political opinions
enter a client's personal data into a tool that uses it to train its models

paras: We choose a tool only when we understand what it does with the data it receives. Tools that process personal data are hosted in Switzerland or the European Union and are covered by a data processing agreement. The tools currently in use are listed on our privacy page.
This policy was last updated on 28 September 2026. Any change is dated and published on this page.

sections.lead: Tribea is a political communication agency in Switzerland. Its team combines people who build digital tools with people who know Swiss campaign and data protection law.

sections.h2: Our policy on clients and conflicts
sections.intro: We work for political actors and for administrations. These rules keep that possible.

items.text: We never advise two opposing camps in the same election or vote.
If a new mandate could conflict with an existing one, we tell both clients before accepting it, or we decline it.

items.h3: No work that breaks our rules

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.description: Tribea's privacy policy under the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection.

sections.lead: This policy explains which personal data we process through this website, why, where it is stored, who receives it, how long it is kept and how you can exercise your rights under the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP).

paras: Tribea, Switzerland. For any question about data protection, write to us through the contact form on this website.

When you open a page, the server records the technical data needed to deliver it and to protect the site: the date and time, the page requested, the browser type and an IP address truncated so that it no longer identifies you. These records are kept only as long as the security of the site requires, then deleted.
Our visitor statistics use the same truncated data, set no cookies and are only read as totals.

When you write to us, we process your name, your email address, your organisation if you give it, and your message, only to answer your request. We keep this correspondence only as long as answering it requires, unless it leads to a mandate, in which case the retention rules of the mandate apply.

If you subscribe, we process your email address to send you our notes. Your subscription is confirmed by a second email, and we keep the date, source and wording of your consent. You can unsubscribe at any time with the link in every message.

Your data is processed by the service providers listed on our privacy page, which act on our behalf under a data processing agreement. The website and its data are hosted in Switzerland, and some services may process data in the European Union, which Switzerland recognises as providing adequate data protection.

You can ask us which data we hold about you, have it corrected or deleted, and object to its processing, by writing to us through the contact form. If you believe we have not respected the law, you can contact the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).
This policy was last updated on 28 September 2026.

articles.title: What the federal transparency rules require of campaigns
articles.description: Since 23 October 2022, parties and campaign committees at federal level have to disclose their financing. A short summary of who is concerned and what must be declared.

paras: Since 23 October 2022, the Federal Act on Political Rights requires political actors at federal level to disclose how they are financed. The Swiss Federal Audit Office receives the declarations, checks them and publishes them.

Parties represented in the Federal Assembly must disclose their income every year, and name any donor who gave more than CHF 15,000 in a year. Committees and other actors who spend more than CHF 50,000 on a campaign for a federal vote or for election to the National Council must declare their budget and the donations above the same threshold.

blocks.h2: What it means for a campaign
paras: In practice, a campaign has to know from its first franc who gave what and when, because the declaration is due before the vote and the final accounts after it. A campaign that records donations only at the end has to reconstruct them under time pressure.
Several cantons have their own transparency rules for cantonal votes and elections, with different thresholds and deadlines, which have to be checked separately.

sources.label: Federal Act on Political Rights, art. 76b to 76d
Swiss Federal Audit Office, political financing

articles.title: Supporter databases and the Federal Act on Data Protection
articles.description: A list of supporters reveals their political opinions, which the law treats as sensitive data. What that changes for a party or a committee.

paras: A list of a party's members, donors or volunteers says something about the political opinions of every person on it. The Federal Act on Data Protection, in force since 1 September 2023, classifies data on political opinions as sensitive personal data.

Sensitive data calls for more care than ordinary contact details. When a processing is likely to create a high risk for the people concerned, the controller has to carry out a data protection impact assessment beforehand. Companies with more than 250 employees, and any organisation processing sensitive data on a large scale, have to keep a record of processing activities. A data breach that is likely to create a high risk has to be reported to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner as soon as possible.

blocks.h2: What it means for a campaign
paras: In practice, a supporter database should hold only the fields its purpose needs, be accessible only to the people who work with it, and be hosted by a provider bound by a data processing agreement. Writing down why each field exists, before the first entry, is also the quickest way to answer a supporter who asks what you hold about them.

sources.label: Federal Act on Data Protection, art. 5, 12, 22 and 24
